Are the audit artifacts any use?

Y:\home\bjieyong\aiverify2\auditing\cv_annotation\audit_bccdp_ground_truth scored against planted errors: missing images had boxes deleted, wrong images had boxes relabelled. Each perturbed image's clean original is in the same set. Review budget = 41 images (the length of review_list.csv).

Sanity checks

  • Images: 414 (364 clean, 25 wrong, 25 missing); every perturbed image has its clean source in the set.
  • Planted boxes: 201 parsed, 201 in the log (ok)
  • Shuffled-score control: AUC 0.543 (expect about 0.5)
  • review_list.csv (41 images: 19 wrong, 13 missing, 9 clean) matches the top 41 of all_ranked.csv
  • Detector training split: 50 of 50 perturbed images are copies of training images; 73 clean images were held out (val).

Verdict per method

Suggestion: keep if AUC (any error) ≥ 0.75 and the paired Δ is positive; drop if AUC < 0.6 or the paired Δ ≤ 0; otherwise down-weight. These thresholds are rough rules of thumb, not tuned.

8. Train/val leakage

Are the results inflated because the detectors saw these images in training?

On 7 of 9 rows, clean training images look less suspicious than clean held-out images: the detectors agree more with labels they were trained on. All 50 perturbed images are copies of training images, so every number in this report measures the audit on images the detectors memorised. Expect weaker results on unseen data; plant errors in held-out images to measure that.
